#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides
#                              it) matches this grep -E pattern -- the hook
#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
#                        (negative-control knob).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# In-ROI verdict check: the guest printed its result on the vsim leg's UART.
if [ -n "${CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT:-}" ]; then
  if grep -qE "$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT" "$SIM_LOG"; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE vsim-stdout] PASS: matched '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
  else
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim output did not match '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
    echo "--- sim log (tail) ---"
    tail -25 "$SIM_LOG"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Negative test: a corrupted --resume-from-qemu state file must trigger a
# fail-fast in vsim with a recognizable error message, not a segfault, hang,
# or silent forward run on garbage state.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

BAD_STATE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$BAD_STATE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT

# 32 bytes of zeros: shorter than hybrid_state_v1, hits the short-read branch.
dd if=/dev/zero of="$BAD_STATE" bs=32 count=1 status=none

set +e
timeout 10 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$BAD_STATE" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

# 0    - silent pass on garbage (BAD)
# 124  - bash timeout fired -> vsim hung (BAD)
# 200  - hybrid handoff exit (BAD: drain ran, state was treated as valid)
# else - any non-zero error path (OK)
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 124 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: expected non-zero, non-200, non-timeout exit; got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if ! grep -Eq "short read|bad magic|cannot open" "$SIM_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: stderr did not match 'short read|bad magic|cannot open'"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[rt_corrupt_state] PASS: vsim fail-fast with rc=$RC"

# Negative test (LM content transport, ROADMAP_ilm_dlm F4a): with the sidecar

  echo "FAIL[rt_lm_transport_off]: fixture PASSED with the transport off" \

  echo "FAIL[rt_lm_transport_off]: expected an in-ROI DLM_BAD verdict; output:"
  printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | tail -20

fi

echo "[rt_lm_transport_off] PASS: transport-off run fails with DLM_BAD as designed"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
# by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
# but are not in active CTest. All targets now share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# v5: L2C-drain fixture -- writes the L2C Control Register, then drains (marker).
l2c_drain.elf: l2c_drain.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c l2c_drain.S -o l2c_drain.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) l2c_drain.o -o $@

# v6: write-mask fixture -- writes a mask-governed CSR, then drains (marker).
wm_drain.elf: wm_drain.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c wm_drain.S -o wm_drain.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) wm_drain.o -o $@

# LM transport (F1): writes the ILM/DLM slave-port windows, then drains (marker).
lm_drain.elf: lm_drain.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c lm_drain.S -o lm_drain.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) lm_drain.o -o $@

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content from the hart-local TCM
# view on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

# QEMU_LM_ARGS also syncs QEMU's LM GEOMETRY to the engine (-global): QEMU's
# compiled-in default is a 2 MB ILM at 0x0, which SHADOWS the program image at
# 0x100000 the moment a guest sets milmb.EN -- with the engine's real 64 KB
# the overlay ends at 0xFFFF and TCM fixtures are safe. (The driver path gets
# the same sync via --print-qemu-config/-readconfig; this mirrors it.)
VSIM_LM_ARGS=()
QEMU_LM_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${ILM_SIZE:-}" ] && [ "$ILM_SIZE" -gt 0 ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,ilm_size=$ILM_SIZE"
  VSIM_LM_ARGS+=(--ilm "$STATE_QEMU.ilm")
  QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=ilm_size,value=$ILM_SIZE")
fi
if [ -n "${DLM_SIZE:-}" ] && [ "$DLM_SIZE" -gt 0 ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,dlm_size=$DLM_SIZE"
  VSIM_LM_ARGS+=(--dlm "$STATE_QEMU.dlm")
  QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=dlm_size,value=$DLM_SIZE")
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm): vsim's --ilm/--dlm backdoor load must land in the RTL
# local memories and SURVIVE elaboration (sc_start) + sim.reset(), so the
# guest reads the loaded content through the hart-local TCM view.
#
#   Run 1: --ilm/--dlm with pattern .bins -> lm_readback exits 0.
#   Run 2 (negative control): no --ilm/--dlm -> TCM is reset-empty -> the
#          SAME fixture exits nonzero (proves the probe really reads TCM).
#
# Premium-engine geometry (the default VSIM_BIN): ILM 64KB, DLM 32KB. The
# pattern offsets mirror lm_readback.c's probes: ILM head 0x10 / tail 0xFFFC,
# DLM head 0x0 / tail 0x7FFC (bin offsets are window-relative).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_BIN   sim_ax45mpv_premium
#   VSIM_ELF   the lm_readback fixture (FIXTURE=lm_readback)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_readback}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

put_word_le() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 32-bit value
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0x10))   $((0x494C4D30))   # ILM head

truncate -s 32768 "$WORK/dlm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" 0           $((0x444C4D30))   # DLM head
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" $((0x7FFC)) $((0x444C4D31))   # DLM tail

---
name: pipe-swallows-build-exit-code
description: Piping a build to tail/head swallows its exit code; use pipefail or no pipe, and verify the log for errors before trusting "exit 0"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`bash build_vsim.sh 2>&1 | tail -5` returns tail's exit code (0), not the
build's. Two vsim rebuilds in one session reported "completed exit 0" while
ninja had actually stopped on a compile error -- the stale binaries then sent
debugging in circles for ~30 minutes.

**Why:** a pipeline's exit code is the LAST command's. `tail` always exits 0,
so any `build | tail` looks successful.

**How to apply:**
- When piping a build (especially `run_in_background` where only the exit code
  comes back), prefix `set -o pipefail`, or don't pipe at all and read the
  output file afterward.
- On any "successful" build, if downstream behavior looks stale (old binary
  semantics, missing symbols/strings), grep the build log for
  `error|build stopped` BEFORE debugging the code. Check `.ninja_log` /
  object-file mtimes to confirm the target actually recompiled.
- This applies to the vsim container build (`build_vsim.sh`, [[andes-engine-config-source]]
  relates: engines are rebuilt per config) and any long build piped for brevity.

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text: 4 個 review agents（reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude）平行跑中，各自拿到兩個 repo 的 session diff。完成會通知，之後我 dedup 並套用修復。

<tool-use-id>toolu_01Pwhw36doWQUwzgYf9N7kpe</tool-use-id>

Evidence for the specifically-requested judgements (all measured/verified, none survive materiality):

- tests/e2e.sh `--describe` probe (andesim: tests/e2e.sh:~866): measured 2.4-4.3 ms per exec on the real 30 MB `sim_ax45mpv_premium` (10-run sample, warm — and it is always warm inside a suite run since the same binary runs the vsim leg). `describe_engine` exits during flag parsing, before any Verilator elaboration, so binary size is irrelevant (demand paging; 6 MB RSS). Real cost: 46 invocations/suite x ~3 ms ≈ 0.14 s spread across the parallel pool, in a suite that runs many minutes. An env passthrough from run_e2e.sh would save ~0.1 s/suite — not worth the code. Note rt_lm_transport_off already skips the probe (sets ILM_SIZE=0 DLM_SIZE=0).
- qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c `drain_lm_sidecar` (andesim diff ~line 644): unsized `g_byte_array_new()` + one 64 KB/32 KB read + write, at most 2 calls per process lifetime. `g_byte_array_sized_new(size)` would avoid a few reallocs; sub-millisecond total — immaterial.
- vsim get_ilm/get_dlm by-value return (vsim: src/cpu_wrappers/ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp:27,80): NRVO applies (single named `out` returned), consumed by const-ref in `dump_lm_sidecars`; once per run at exit, 96 KB — inside the stated materiality bar.
- driver/run_plan.cpp:522 lm scan: folded into the pre-existing accurate-leg/vlen loop (no new pass), once per plan build — zero added cost.
- test_vsim_lm_load.sh double vsim run: measured a full run-1 (`--ilm/--dlm` + lm_readback) at 1.38 s wall (rc=0). The negative-control second run costs ~1.4 s in a manual, not-suite-wired test. Folding both into one `--ilm`-only run (assert exit 3) would drop the isolated set_dlm-positive coverage to save ~1.4 s — not worth it.
- rt_lm_transport_off full e2e re-run: one extra hybrid run per suite (~1 of 48 slots in the parallel pool). Its purpose — observing DLM_BAD from a real vsim leg resumed on real QEMU1 state with the transport off — cannot be met more cheaply: e2e.sh has no state-reuse mode, and the QEMU1 leg it would skip is the cheap (MHz) leg anyway. Not avoidable without weakening or new plumbing that costs more than it saves.</result>

```cpp
template <int DataWidth, int EccType>
static std::vector<uint8_t> lm_read(auto& mem, size_t bytes) {
  constexpr size_t word_size = DataWidth == 64 ? 8 : 4;
  using word_t = std::conditional_t<DataWidth == 64, uint64_t, uint32_t>;
  std::vector<uint8_t> out(bytes);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes / word_size; ++i) {
    word_t word;
    if constexpr (EccType == 2 && DataWidth == 64)
      word = word_t(mem[i][0]) | (word_t(mem[i][1]) << 32);
    else if constexpr (EccType == 2) word = word_t(mem[i] & 0xFFFFFFFFull);
    else                             word = word_t(mem[i]);
    for (size_t j = 0; j < word_size; ++j)
      out[i * word_size + j] = uint8_t(word >> (j * 8));
  }
  return out;
}
// get_ilm(): auto& mem = <existing #ifdef path>;
//            return lm_read<NDS_ILM_DATA_WIDTH, _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT>(mem, SIZE);
```
`if constexpr` on template params keeps discarded branches uninstantiated, so the VlWide `[0]/[1]` indexing never touches the scalar-typed configs — same trick `load_image` already uses with `requires`. This respects the `#define SIZE` blocks (SIZE is just the call argument).
Judgment on scope: worth doing for the read side only. Do NOT extend the dedup to set_ilm/set_dlm in this change - the write side has different per-config forms (`VL_SET_WQ`, ECC generation), is pre-existing behavior, and per Tidy First belongs to a separate structural commit if ever. The counterargument (match the file's set_* copy-paste style) buys symmetry but pays 35 duplicated lines of the one genuinely error-prone loop; a future parity variant (`ECC_TYPE 1`) would need editing 2 places or silently diverge.

if [ -z "${ILM_SIZE:-}" ] || [ -z "${DLM_SIZE:-}" ]; then
  DESCRIBE_JSON=$("$VSIM_BIN" --describe 2>/dev/null || true)
  probe_size() { printf '%s' "$DESCRIBE_JSON" \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1; }
  ILM_SIZE=${ILM_SIZE:-$(probe_size ilm_size)}
  DLM_SIZE=${DLM_SIZE:-$(probe_size dlm_size)}
fi
VSIM_LM_ARGS=(); QEMU_LM_ARGS=()
lm_wire() {  # $1 ilm|dlm, $2 size (bytes)
  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0

template <int DataWidth, int EccType>
static std::vector<uint8_t> lm_read(auto& mem, size_t bytes) {
  constexpr size_t word_size = DataWidth == 64 ? 8 : 4;
  using word_t = std::conditional_t<DataWidth == 64, uint64_t, uint32_t>;
  std::vector<uint8_t> out(bytes);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes / word_size; ++i) {

    else if constexpr (EccType == 2) word = word_t(mem[i] & 0xFFFFFFFFull);
    else                             word = word_t(mem[i]);
    for (size_t j = 0; j < word_size; ++j)

  }
  return out;

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Syscalls: all C-level fixtures link the vplat runtime
 * (build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a, no semihosting): newlib stdio
 * bottoms out in the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io in the SimControl
 * device, which BOTH engines model. A syscall inside the
 * enter_vsim()/exit_vsim() span therefore works on vsim too -- it just
 * adds its real cycles (UART polling, dcache flush) to the measured
 * figure, so cycle-measuring fixtures keep the span syscall-free by
 * choice, not by rule.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then

  done
}

  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"

    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm): vsim's --ilm/--dlm backdoor load must land in the RTL
# local memories and SURVIVE elaboration (sc_start) + sim.reset(), so the
# guest reads the loaded content through the hart-local TCM view.
#
#   Run 1: --ilm/--dlm with pattern .bins -> lm_readback exits 0.
#   Run 2 (negative control): no --ilm/--dlm -> TCM is reset-empty -> the
#          SAME fixture exits nonzero (proves the probe really reads TCM).
#
# Premium-engine geometry (the default VSIM_BIN): ILM 64KB, DLM 32KB. The
# pattern offsets mirror lm_readback.c's probes: ILM head 0x10 / tail 0xFFFC,
# DLM head 0x0 / tail 0x7FFC (bin offsets are window-relative).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_BIN   sim_ax45mpv_premium
#   VSIM_ELF   the lm_readback fixture (FIXTURE=lm_readback)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_readback}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

put_word_le() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 32-bit value
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

truncate -s 65536 "$WORK/ilm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0x10))   $((0x494C4D30))   # ILM head
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0xFFFC)) $((0x494C4D31))   # ILM tail
truncate -s 32768 "$WORK/dlm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" 0           $((0x444C4D30))   # DLM head
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" $((0x7FFC)) $((0x444C4D31))   # DLM tail

# --- Run 1: loaded TCM -> probe passes ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" --ilm "$WORK/ilm.bin" --dlm "$WORK/dlm.bin" \
  "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run1.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe exit=$RC (1=ILM head, 2=ILM tail, 3=DLM head, 4=DLM tail)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run1.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Run 2: negative control, empty TCM -> the same probe must FAIL ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run2.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe passed with NO --ilm/--dlm (reads are not hitting TCM)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run2.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Describe gating: ilm_size/dlm_size advertise the LM TRANSPORT, so they
# must be non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_ilm/set_dlm
# backdoor. Premium has it (real sizes); ax46mpv_advanced's config has the
# memories but its wrapper lacks the backdoor -> must report 0, or the driver
# would pass --ilm/--dlm and load_image would throw (the F3 ax46 regression).
DESC=$("$VSIM_BIN" --describe 2>/dev/null || true)
if ! printf '%s' "$DESC" | grep -q '"ilm_size": 65536, "dlm_size": 32768'; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"
  exit 1
fi
AX46="$(dirname "$VSIM_BIN")/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  D46=$("$AX46" --describe 2>/dev/null || true)
  if ! printf '%s' "$D46" | grep -q '"ilm_size": 0, "dlm_size": 0'; then
    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

echo "PASS[vsim_lm_load]"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "ilm_size": 65536,
  "dlm_size": 32768,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "jvt"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `ilm_size` | number          | no       | Hart-0 ILM size in BYTES (0 / omit = none). When > 0, a hybrid run drains the ILM content to a `<state>.ilm` sidecar on the fast leg and feeds it to the accurate leg via `--ilm` (same for `dlm_size`/`--dlm`). |
| `dlm_size` | number          | no       | Hart-0 DLM size in BYTES (0 / omit = none). |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{trigger}`   | the plugin comma-suffix: trigger args (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) plus, when the accurate engine reports local memories, the LM sidecar-drain args (`,ilm_size=N,dlm_size=N`) |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
   present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
   `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.
5. **(Optional) QEMU ISA match**: implement `--print-qemu-config` to emit a QEMU `-readconfig` cfg (per-extension `[global]` properties) describing your engine's ISA, so a hybrid run's QEMU fast leg executes the same extensions you model. On a hybrid run the framework runs `<accurate-engine> --print-qemu-config` and passes the result to QEMU via `-readconfig`. If you do not implement it (the flag exits non-zero), the framework falls back to QEMU's default `-cpu` -- no error. vsim bakes this cfg from its `config.inc` at build time.

Suite 背景跑。等結果時整理 simplify pass 的帳目（12 個 findings 的處置）：

## 已套用（10）

**andesim：**
1. **enable_ilm/enable_dlm 共用 helper**（reuse#4 + simplification）- 3 個 fixture 的 4 份 CSR-RMW 貼片收進 `rt_c_helpers.h`
2. **lm_drain.S 用 `HART0_ILM_BASE/HART0_DLM_BASE`**（reuse#3）- 吃現成 `memory_map.h`，不再硬編
3. **`hybrid_describe_int` 進 paths.sh**（reuse#5 + altitude#4）- descriptor 的 shell parser 收成一份；`test_vsim_lm_load.sh` 改斷言「值」而非 JSON 排版（describe 改排版不再誤殺）
4. **e2e.sh `lm_wire()` 折疊**（simplification）- ilm/dlm 四份貼片收成一個函式，三個接線目標各一行
5. **EXIT trap 用 glob**（simplification）- `"$STATE_QEMU".*` 蓋掉未來任何 sidecar 後綴
6. **`drain_lm_sidecar` 用 `g_strdup_printf`**（simplification）- 刪掉手滾 PATH_MAX 檢查和人造錯誤分支
7. **Makefile 三條 probe fixture 規則合一**（simplification）- rule-of-three 觸發
8. **json_test 併進共用 absent block**（simplification）
9. **`{plugin_args}` placeholder + `{trigger}` 為相容別名**（altitude#5）- 名字不再說謊，第三方 template 不破

**vsim：**
10. **三合一 altitude 修**（altitude#2+#3 + reuse#1+#2 + simplification）：
   - `kCpuCanLoad/DumpIlm/Dlm` 變數模板收進 simulator.hpp 當**單一權威**，`load_image`/`dump_lm_sidecars`/describe 全部改讀它 - 廣告側和載入側永不漂移
   - describe gating 改成 **load AND dump** - 修掉 agent 抓到的真缺口：d23/d25fse 這種「有 set_ 沒 get_」的 wrapper 原本會廣告 transport 然後 exit dump 靜默缺檔

- **`ilm_base=/dlm_base=` plugin knob 無 caller**（simplification，最弱項）- 跟一行之隔的 `l2c_base` 同款 house style，留。
- **e2e.sh `-global` vs driver `-readconfig` 雙機制**（altitude#1，最大項）- deeper form 是 e2e.sh 改吃 qemu.cfg，但那會讓 **每個** e2e fixture 的 ISA/vlen 語意跟著變，是一次需要自己驗證計畫的套件級改動，超出本 diff 範圍。已寫進 ROADMAP「Known altitude debt」段（含 `*_default_enable` 分歧和 negative-knob 連動幾何的陷阱）。

content.text:
誠實答案：**只測到一半 - QEMU 側有，vsim RTL 側沒有**。這是個很準的問題。

## 每條路徑對照這個 region

| 路徑 | 走 0xA0000000 aperture 嗎? | 有測? |
|------|------------------------|-------|
| QEMU: guest store（lm_drain.S） | 是 - 直接寫 0xA0000000/0xA0200000，走 `subport_ops` dispatch | 有（`test_plugin_lm_drain`） |
| QEMU: plugin drain | 是 - `read_memory_hwaddr(0xA0000000)`，每次 LM hybrid run 都走 | 有（所有 LM e2e） |
| QEMU: local-view 寫 <-> slave-port 讀 aliasing | 是 - rt_c_* 用 0x100/0x200000 寫、plugin 從 0xA... 讀 | 有 |
| **vsim: transport in**（`set_ilm`） | **否 - Verilator backdoor 直捅 SRAM 陣列，不走 bus** | - |
| **vsim: ROI 存取**（fetch 0x100 / read 0x200000） | **否 - hart-local view，core 內部路徑** | - |
| **vsim: transport out**（`get_ilm`） | **否 - backdoor 讀** | - |
| **vsim: interconnect -> `slv_bfm` -> TCM 路由** | 這才是 vsim 的 0xA0000000 region 本體（`simulator.hpp:157-168` 綁 `{HART0_ILM_BASE, HART0_DLM_END}`） | **沒有 committed test** |

## 意思是

**vsim 那邊，我們測的是「local memory 的內容 + hart-local view」，不是「slave port 這個 region」。** 如果 vsim 的 interconnect 到 `slv_bfm` 的路由整個是壞的，今天全套 48 個 test 照樣全綠。第一個發現的會是 DMA-into-TCM 這類外部 master 的 workload。

兩個誠實的補充：
1. F2 debug 時我的**丟棄式 probe** 曾在 vsim 上讀過一次 `0xA0000010`（hart 發 load -> bus -> slv_bfm -> ILM）且通過 - 所以 ILM 那條路由**大概率是通的**，但那是 scratchpad 代碼，沒進 repo；**DLM 的 slave-port 路由連一次都沒被讀過**。
2. QEMU 側也只覆蓋前 `ilm_size`(64KB)/`dlm_size`(32KB) - aperture 剩下的 ~1.9MB（RAM backing 之外的 subport 行為）和 hart 1-7 的 subports 都沒測（後者是 R4 明定的單 hart 範圍）。

## 補洞成本很低

`lm_readback.c` 加 4 個 probe（`0xA0000010`/`0xA000FFFC`/`0xA0200000`/`0xA0207FFC`）就能讓 F2 test 順便驗 vsim 的 slave-port 路由 - hart 自己走 aperture 存取在 vsim 上就是 bus -> slv_bfm 迴路，debug probe 已證明可行。要補嗎？

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm): vsim's --ilm/--dlm backdoor load must land in the RTL
# local memories and SURVIVE elaboration (sc_start) + sim.reset(), so the
# guest reads the loaded content through the hart-local TCM view.
#
#   Run 1: --ilm/--dlm with pattern .bins -> lm_readback exits 0.
#   Run 2 (negative control): no --ilm/--dlm -> TCM is reset-empty -> the
#          SAME fixture exits nonzero (proves the probe really reads TCM).
#
# Premium-engine geometry (the default VSIM_BIN): ILM 64KB, DLM 32KB. The
# pattern offsets mirror lm_readback.c's probes: ILM head 0x10 / tail 0xFFFC,
# DLM head 0x0 / tail 0x7FFC (bin offsets are window-relative).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_BIN   sim_ax45mpv_premium
#   VSIM_ELF   the lm_readback fixture (FIXTURE=lm_readback)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_readback}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

put_word_le() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 32-bit value
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

truncate -s 65536 "$WORK/ilm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0x10))   $((0x494C4D30))   # ILM head
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0xFFFC)) $((0x494C4D31))   # ILM tail
truncate -s 32768 "$WORK/dlm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" 0           $((0x444C4D30))   # DLM head
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" $((0x7FFC)) $((0x444C4D31))   # DLM tail

# --- Run 1: loaded TCM -> probe passes ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" --ilm "$WORK/ilm.bin" --dlm "$WORK/dlm.bin" \
  "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run1.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe exit=$RC (1=ILM head, 2=ILM tail, 3=DLM head, 4=DLM tail)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run1.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Run 2: negative control, empty TCM -> the same probe must FAIL ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run2.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe passed with NO --ilm/--dlm (reads are not hitting TCM)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run2.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Describe gating: ilm_size/dlm_size advertise the LM TRANSPORT, so they
# must be non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_ilm/set_dlm
# backdoor. Premium has it (real sizes); ax46mpv_advanced's config has the
# memories but its wrapper lacks the backdoor -> must report 0, or the driver
# would pass --ilm/--dlm and load_image would throw (the F3 ax46 regression).
# Field extraction rides the shared hybrid_describe_int (paths.sh), so this
# asserts VALUES, not the descriptor's JSON formatting.
if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)" != 65536 ] \
   || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)" != 32768 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"
  exit 1
fi
AX46="$(dirname "$VSIM_BIN")/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ] \
     || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

echo "PASS[vsim_lm_load]"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
# by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
# but are not in active CTest. All targets now share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content from the hart-local TCM
# view on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

aiTitle: 探索 hybrid mode 對 AE350 memory map 的支援

content.text:
讀完 `subport_read/write` 本體了。一句話：**QEMU 把 slave port 做成 16 個「轉發器」- 不存資料，只把任何打到 0xA0xxxxxx 的 system-bus 存取，轉發進目標 hart 私有的 TCM RAM**。

## 結構（`andes_ae350.c:1293-1399`）

```
system memory (全域 bus 視角)
  0xA0000000  subport0_ilm  {hart_id=0, dlm=false}   <- 2MB IO region
  0xA0200000  subport0_dlm  {hart_id=0, dlm=true}
  0xA0400000  subport1_ilm  {hart_id=1, ...}         <- 每個 hart 佔 4MB
  ...共 8 個 hart x 2

subport_read(opaque, addr, size):
  cs  = qemu_get_cpu(s->hart_id)              // 找到目標 hart
  env = &RISCV_CPU(cs)->env
  memory_region_dispatch_read(env->mask_ilm,  // 直接打進那顆 CPU 的
      addr, &ret, size, ...)                  // 私有 TCM RAM
```

關鍵：真正的儲存體是 **per-CPU 的 `env->mask_ilm/mask_dlm`**（`memory_region_init_ram`，掛在該 CPU 私有的 `cpu_as_root`）。subport 只是 system memory 上的門面，用 `memory_region_dispatch_*` **繞過 address space 直接戳那塊 RAM**。

## Usage - 誰會走這個門

1. **別的 hart**：hart 1 寫 `0xA0000000` = 寫進 hart 0 的 ILM（跨 hart 灌 code 的標準做法）。
2. **DMA / device model**：任何對 system memory 做 `address_space_rw` 的 master。
3. **我們的 plugin**：`qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr(0xA0000000)` 走 CPU 的 AS，0xA0 區沒被 local overlay 蓋住，落到 system memory -> subport -> 目標 hart 的 TCM。這就是 drain 的路。
4. **hart 自己**：自己 load/store `0xA0000000` 也會繞出去再轉回自己的 TCM（`lm_drain.S` 就是這樣）。

## 三個從 code 直接掉出來的語義

- **不看 `milmb.EN`**：EN 只控制「local view overlay 掛不掛進 CPU 自己的 AS」（`cpu.c:680` 的 `add_subregion_overlap` 有 `if (env->ilm_default_enable)` gate）；subport 是直接 dispatch 到 `mask_ilm`，只要 `ilm_size>0` 那塊 RAM 就存在。**所以 EN=0 時外部照樣能先灌 TCM，之後 hart 再開 EN 來用** - 跟真硬體的 bring-up 順序一致，也解釋了為什麼 `lm_drain` 在 EN=off 的 raw QEMU 路徑能過。
- **1-8 byte、可 unaligned**（`subport_ops.valid/.impl`）。
- **hart 不存在**（`qemu_get_cpu` 回 NULL）：讀到 0、寫被丟掉，不會炸。

一個誠實的邊界：window 是固定 2MB，但 `mask_ilm` 只有 `ilm_size`(64KB)- **超過 64KB 的 offset 會 dispatch 到 RAM region 範圍外**，那個行為（error? 0?）我沒讀 `memory_region_dispatch_read` 的深處、也沒測，這正是 ROADMAP 記的「aperture 超出 RAM-backed 部分未測」。

## 對照 vsim

| | QEMU | vsim |
|---|---|---|
| slave port 本體 | IO 轉發器 -> per-CPU RAM | interconnect 路由 -> `slv_bfm`（RTL 真線路） |
| storage | `mask_ilm`（host RAM 一塊） | Verilated SRAM 陣列 |
| EN 影響 slave port? | 否 | 否（RTL 的 slave port 也是獨立 port） |

兩邊語義對得上，這也是為什麼 transport 選 slave-port 位址當 drain 視窗是穩的。

現在可以精確回答了，含一個剛驗證的重要細節。

## 直接答案

**QEMU 自己（machine model、loader、device）從不主動使用 slave port。** 它是純被動的硬體擬真視窗 - 只有「guest 程式自己定址 0xA0xxxxxx」或「外部工具」時才會被走到。QEMU 建它的目的，是讓真 Andes 韌體的以下情境不用改就能跑：

## 會用到它的四個真實情境

1. **多 hart 開機 staging（這個 port 存在的硬體理由）**：hart 0 的 boot 韌體把 hart 1..7 要跑的 code 透過各自的 subport（`0xA0400000`、`0xA0800000`...）灌進**別顆 hart** 的 ILM，再喚醒它們。TCM 是 per-hart 私有的，slave port 是唯一能從外面碰到它的門。

2. **Preload-before-enable**：`milmb.EN=0` 時 hart-local 視窗根本不存在（0x0 打到的是 DRAM），**slave port 是唯一能碰到 TCM 的位址**。韌體先從 slave port 灌內容、再開 EN。我們的 `lm_drain.S` 就是這個 pattern（EN=off 的 raw QEMU 下照樣能寫能讀）。

3. **Debugger**：gdb 對 physical address 的讀寫（gdbstub 走 system memory）。

4. **我們的 plugin**（這 session 新增的使用者）：`qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr(0xA0000000)` drain。

另外 IOPMP 的 protect-region 表（`andes_ae350.c:849,859-860`）把這段列為**可保護目標** - 那是「別人存取它時被 IOPMP 攔」的配置，不是主動使用。

## 剛驗證到的一個地雷（QEMU loader 不但不用，還會靜默丟棄）

`address_space_write_rom`（`system/physmem.c:3512-3519`）- ELF/-bios 載入的寫入路徑 - 對非 RAM region 的處理是：

```c
if (!memory_region_supports_direct_access(mr)) {
    l = memory_access_size(mr, l, addr1);   // 算個長度...
}                                            // ...然後什麼都不寫，直接跳過
```

所以**一個把 section LMA 放在 0xA0000000 的 ELF，用 `-bios` 載入時那段 bytes 會被靜默丟掉** - 不報錯、不落地。這反向確認了兩件事：(a) loader 這條路徑不是 slave port 的使用者；(b) 我們 F4 選「runtime 由程式自己灌 TCM」而不是 linker section 是唯一正確的做法 - 就算當時想走 linker 路線，也會在這裡靜默失敗。

# F2 (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm): vsim's --ilm/--dlm backdoor load must land in the RTL
# local memories and SURVIVE elaboration (sc_start) + sim.reset(), so the
# guest reads the loaded content through the hart-local TCM view AND through
# the local-memory slave-port aperture (0xA0000000/0xA0200000 -- the probe's
# aperture loads are the only exercise of the vsim interconnect->slv_bfm
# routing; the transport itself uses backdoor pokes on this side).
#
#   Run 1: --ilm/--dlm with pattern .bins -> lm_readback exits 0.
#   Run 2 (negative control): no --ilm/--dlm -> TCM is reset-empty -> the
#          SAME fixture exits nonzero (proves the probe really reads TCM).
#
# Premium-engine geometry (the default VSIM_BIN): ILM 64KB, DLM 32KB. The
# pattern offsets mirror lm_readback.c's probes: ILM head 0x10 / tail 0xFFFC,
# DLM head 0x0 / tail 0x7FFC (bin offsets are window-relative).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_BIN   sim_ax45mpv_premium
#   VSIM_ELF   the lm_readback fixture (FIXTURE=lm_readback)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_readback}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

put_word_le() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 32-bit value
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

truncate -s 65536 "$WORK/ilm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0x10))   $((0x494C4D30))   # ILM head
put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0xFFFC)) $((0x494C4D31))   # ILM tail
truncate -s 32768 "$WORK/dlm.bin"
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" 0           $((0x444C4D30))   # DLM head
put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" $((0x7FFC)) $((0x444C4D31))   # DLM tail

# --- Run 1: loaded TCM -> probe passes ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" --ilm "$WORK/ilm.bin" --dlm "$WORK/dlm.bin" \
  "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run1.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe exit=$RC (1-4=local view ILM/DLM head/tail," \
       "5=EN no stick, 6-9=slave-port aperture ILM/DLM head/tail)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run1.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Run 2: negative control, empty TCM -> the same probe must FAIL ---
timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run2.log" 2>&1
RC=$?
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe passed with NO --ilm/--dlm (reads are not hitting TCM)"
  tail -15 "$WORK/run2.log"
  exit 1
fi

# --- Describe gating: ilm_size/dlm_size advertise the LM TRANSPORT, so they
# must be non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_ilm/set_dlm
# backdoor. Premium has it (real sizes); ax46mpv_advanced's config has the
# memories but its wrapper lacks the backdoor -> must report 0, or the driver
# would pass --ilm/--dlm and load_image would throw (the F3 ax46 regression).
# Field extraction rides the shared hybrid_describe_int (paths.sh), so this
# asserts VALUES, not the descriptor's JSON formatting.
if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)" != 65536 ] \
   || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)" != 32768 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: premium --describe does not report ilm 65536 / dlm 32768"
  exit 1
fi
AX46="$(dirname "$VSIM_BIN")/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  if [ "$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ] \
     || [ "$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size "$AX46")" != 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

echo "PASS[vsim_lm_load]"

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
