#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Efficiency review — HVM-transport change set

One material finding; the rest of the diff is clean on this axis.

### Finding 1 (primary): `tests/e2e.sh` triples/doubles the per-run engine `--describe` spawns
- **File/lines:** `tests/e2e.sh:137-139` (the `*_SIZE` defaults) + `:158-160` (the new `lm_geom` calls). Helper: `tests/lib/paths.sh:37-40`.
- **Summary:** The geom/wire split re-invokes `hybrid_describe_int` for ilm/dlm/hvm a *second* time (158-160) to feed `lm_geom`, duplicating the exact `--describe` output that lines 137-139 already computed for `ILM_SIZE/DLM_SIZE/HVM_SIZE`.
- **Concrete cost:** Each `hybrid_describe_int` call fork+execs the large Verilated `sim_ax45mpv_premium` binary (`--describe`) plus a `sed`+`head` pipe. Before this change the block spawned the engine **2×** (ilm, dlm). After it spawns **6×** (ilm, dlm, hvm — each computed twice). All six spawns produce byte-identical JSON from the same embedded config blob, and that one JSON already contains all three fields. This block runs once per `e2e.sh` invocation, i.e. once per fixture/trigger-mode — and `run_e2e.sh` fans it across the RT fixtures plus the two negative drivers, so it is ~4 extra heavy binary loads per fixture across the whole suite. Note the redundancy is unconditional on the hot side: lines 158-160 spawn `--describe` even for the negative-control runs (e.g. `rt_hvm_transport_off.sh` with `HVM_SIZE=0`), which the env-override on 137-139 was specifically meant to short-circuit — so the "transport off" path still pays 3 engine spawns it does not use.
- **Cheaper alternative:** Capture the three real describe values once and reuse them for both the `*_SIZE` default and `lm_geom` (the split needs the *engine's* real size, not the env-overridable one, but that value is identical across the two call sites):
  ```
  ILM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size); DLM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size); HVM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)
  ILM_SIZE="${ILM_SIZE:-$ILM_REAL}"; DLM_SIZE="${DLM_SIZE:-$DLM_REAL}"; HVM_SIZE="${HVM_SIZE:-$HVM_REAL}"
  lm_geom ilm "$ILM_REAL"; lm_geom dlm "$DLM_REAL"; lm_geom hvm "$HVM_REAL"
  ```
  → 3 spawns. Better still, since one JSON holds all three fields, capture `--describe` once (`desc=$("$VSIM_BIN" --describe 2>/dev/null)`) and `sed` the three fields out of `$desc` → **1** engine spawn. Ladder: 6 → 3 → 1.

### Checked and NOT flagged (introduce no hot-path waste)
- `hvm_bank_write` / `hvm_bank_read` / `set_hvm` / `get_hvm` (`ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`): the full-256KB byte-by-byte walk runs once per `--hvm` load and once per exit `get_hvm` dump — backdoor operations, not per-iteration/per-cycle paths. `get_hvm`'s 256KB `std::vector` return is RVO/moved; `set_hvm`'s second `hvm_bank_write` uses a pointer offset, no buffer copy. Fine.
- `run_plan.cpp` lm_suffix concatenation and the `lm_geom` hvm log2 shift-loop: trivial, once per plan. Fine.
- `rt_c_hvm_data.c` 256KB fill loop: on the fast QEMU leg and intrinsic to what the fixture stages (the data exists nowhere but HVM by design); ROI reads are deliberately sampled (3 windows) to stay cycle-cheap. Not introduced waste.</result>

- File: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/cpu_wrappers/ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp:662-665`
- `hvm_bank_write(b1, bank_bytes, data.data() + std::min(n, bank_bytes), n > bank_bytes ? n - bank_bytes : 0)` — a `std::min` plus a ternary plus pointer arithmetic just to feed bank1.
- Cost: two off-by-one-prone expressions a reader must verify for out-of-bounds pointer safety; the `min` exists only to keep the pointer in-bounds when `n < bank_bytes`.
- Simpler: `hvm_bank_write` already clamps every byte with `if (idx < len)` and zero-fills. Give it the whole buffer + a base byte offset (`const std::vector<uint8_t>& data, size_t base`, test `base+idx < data.size()`). Callers collapse to `hvm_bank_write(b0, bank_bytes, data, 0);` / `hvm_bank_write(b1, bank_bytes, data, bank_bytes);` — no `n`, `min`, or ternary, and it becomes symmetric with the already-clean `hvm_bank_read` calls (get_hvm:684-685).

- File: `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/e2e.sh:137-139` and `:158-160`

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout

#

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).

cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves

  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# HVM transport F3 (ROADMAP_hvm): the driver arms the HVM content transport
# from the accurate engine's descriptor, exactly like ILM/DLM --
#   fast leg   : plugin args gain ",hvm_size=<bytes>" (sidecar drain)
#   accurate leg: argv gains "--hvm <state_in>.hvm"   (backdoor load)
# and an engine describing hvm_size=0 must arm NEITHER. Asserted through
# `--dry-run`, which prints the exact argvs without running engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# Resolve the vsim engine dir the way the driver does (env, then config.env).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v
  v=$(grep -oP 'VSIM_BIN_DIR=\K.*' "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$ROOT/verilator/build"
}
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
PREMIUM="$BINDIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
if [ ! -x "$PREMIUM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: no sim_ax45mpv_premium under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

# The engine's own advertised size is the wiring's source of truth.
HVM_SIZE=$("$PREMIUM" --describe 2>/dev/null \
           | sed -n 's/.*"hvm_size": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)
[ -n "$HVM_SIZE" ] && [ "$HVM_SIZE" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "premium --describe lacks a non-zero hvm_size (vsim F1 regression?)"

out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
      --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE" \
  || fail "fast-leg plugin args lack hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
  || fail "accurate-leg argv lacks --hvm <state>.hvm: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'ilm_size=' \
  || fail "LM wiring regressed (no ilm_size= in plugin args): $out"
ok "premium: plugin hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE + accurate-leg --hvm armed"

# Negative: an engine that describes hvm_size=0 (ax46: config has HVM, wrapper
# has no backdoor) must arm neither side.
AX46="$BINDIR/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
        --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax46mpv_advanced "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "ax46 hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hvm_size=' \
    && fail "ax46 (hvm_size 0) must not arm the plugin hvm drain: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
    && fail "ax46 (hvm_size 0) must not get --hvm: $out"
  ok "ax46: hvm transport stays off (describe hvm_size=0)"
else
  ok "SKIP ax46 negative: no sim_ax46mpv_advanced under $BINDIR"
fi

echo "PASS[andes_sim_hvm_wiring]"

## 修了的（5）

1. **e2e.sh describe spawn 6 次 → 3 次**（efficiency + simplification 同時抓到）：geometry/transport 分離時我讓每個 memory 各 probe 兩次。現在 `*_REAL` 只 probe 一次，同時餵 `*_SIZE` 預設值和 `lm_geom`。
2. **`put_word_le` 重複兩份**（reuse）：上收到 `tests/lib/paths.sh`，lm 和 hvm 兩個 test 的本地副本刪除。
3. **`vsim_bin_dir` 遮蔽現成的**（reuse）：hvm_wiring test 重刻了 log.sh 已有的 function（我從 dry_run test 抄的 — 那份本身就是舊債），改用 log.sh 的。
4. **`describe | sed` 重刻 wire-format parser**（reuse）：同一個 test 裡違反了 paths.sh 明文的「唯一 parser」約定，改呼叫 `hybrid_describe_int hvm_size "$PREMIUM"`。
5. **wrapper codec 整理**（simplification + altitude C 的便宜部分）：`hvm_bank_write` 改收 `(data, base)` 自己 clamp，呼叫端的 `min`+三元運算指標算式消失、跟 read 對稱；整個 HVM helper 區塊搬到 `lm_backdoor_read` 的註解上方（我原本把那註解跟它的 function 拆散了），並在註解裡寫明**為什麼**不能重用 LM 的 codec（16 lanes/row 的幾何 LM 模板表達不了）— 順帶修正 ROADMAP 裡同一件事的錯誤敘述。

## 跳過的（3，皆記錄）

- **`rt_hvm_transport_off.sh` 與 lm 版合併成參數化腳本**：repo 慣例是一情境一檔（agent 自己也標 low-confidence），跟 LM 當時的決定一致。
- **`lm_geom` 的 `hvm` 分支改成 per-kind 屬性表**（altitude A）：3 kinds / 1 個分歧軸還不到表格的門檻，第 4 個 kind 再說。
- **`lm_*` 改名 `mem_*`**（altitude D）：`CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS` 是 user-facing 的 harness API，半改名更糟。改成把 ROADMAP 的 debt 判準寫死：第 4 個 memory kind 出現時，改名 + 把 8 檔平行修改收斂成單一 per-kind 註冊表，一起做。
